result.title: FishSense Lite: A Camera-Based, Single Laser Hardware Framework with Software System for In Situ Fish Length Measurement
result.summary: Fish stock assessments need fish lengths paired with species from far more places than trained surveyors can reach. Recreational divers already visit many of those places, but measuring a fish underwater has required trained observers or specialist equipment. We present FishSense Lite, which recovers fish length from a single photograph taken with a recreational dive camera, a dive laser pointer, and a 3D-printed mount. The diver aims the laser at a fish and takes a picture; afterward, the dot's position in the image gives the range to the fish, and the range turns the fish's size in the image into a length. A citizen-science program, trained by the system's builders, taught its own divers and collected lengths paired with species for 73 wild fish across seven open-water dives. On seven wild fish also measured by an underwater stereo-imaging system, the two instruments agreed without detectable bias (mean difference +0.8%). On rigid targets of known length, FishSense Lite recovered every target to within 1.3%, and 99% of 1,055 frames fell within a 15% error budget. From the error sources we measure, we derive a field protocol: calibrate against a dive slate on every dive, photograph fish within 15 degrees of perpendicular and beyond 1 m, and take at least ten frames of each.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作提出 FishSense Lite：用休闲潜水相机的单张照片配合潜水激光笔和 3D 打印支架，借激光斑在图像中的位置推算距离，把像中的鱼体尺寸换算为实际体长，并通过公民科学潜水员采集带物种标注的野外数据做验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于水下测量硬件与公民科学数据采集应用，虽涉及单视图几何测距，但没有内部推理状态、证据筛选、动态计算或停止决策等机制，也未讨论 VLM 或 latent 表示，与 LVR 主线缺少可核查的借鉴线索。
